newsitem.title: UK: Computer Cab to float on AIM at 80p on April 4.
newsitem.headline: Computer Cab to float on AIM at 80p on April 4.

text.p: London taxi operator Computer Cab Plc said on Tuesday it plans to float its shares on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market via a placing at 80p. First dealings are scheduled for April 4.
At the placing price, the company, which said it was the UK's largest taxi operator with 2,100 drivers, said it would have a market capitalisation of 8.25 million stg.

The issue will raise 3.3 million after expenses which will be used to reduce borrowing, increase working capital and fund the installation and marketing of the company's Mobistar automatic vehicle location and taxi dispatch system.

Computer Cab said it expected to invest a total of 7.8 million stg in its Mobistar system, which is based on Global Positioning Satellite technology. The company has already invested over 6.5 million stg in Mobistar.
Computer Cab's managing director Geof Kaley said the float was an important development for the company.

"The flotation is a significant step in the development of Computer Cab," Kaley said in a statement. "Mobistar's leading-edge technology and the ownership of shares in the company by our drivers will further strengthen our business and market position."
Computer Cab said it intended to consider opportunities for expansion outside of London, both in the UK and internationally.
The nominated broker to the issue is Branston & Gothard Ltd.
